title: Compliance-anchored rollback and evidence preservation playbook
author: Asha Kapoor
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines a compliance-first rollback process for Redwood Private deployments and prescribes steps to preserve, collect, and sign evidentiary artifacts during and after rollback operations. It is intended for field operators, on-call SREs, and the security/compliance owners who must produce an auditable trail following a rollback for regulated customers.

Scope:
- Applies to private deployments (VPC and on-prem) running Redwood runtime services and control plane components.
- Covers planned and emergency rollbacks that revert deployed software, model bundles, or configuration changes.
- Excludes: customer-managed third-party components outside the deployment boundary unless contractually required.

Audience:
- Field Operators / Deployment Engineers
- SRE and Oncall teams
- Security & Compliance reviewers
- Customer Success leads for affected customers

Key goals:
- Ensure rollback actions are reversible and attributable.
- Preserve tamper-evident artifacts (logs, manifests, checksums, signatures).
- Minimize customer downtime while meeting legal/regulatory evidence obligations.

Roles & ownership

- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates rollback execution and communications. (Owner: oncall SRE)
- Evidence Custodian: responsible for collecting, hashing, signing, and storing artifacts in the evidence store. (Owner: Security)
- Deployment Lead: executes the technical rollback steps; creates manifests of actions taken. (Owner: Field Ops / Operator team)
- Customer Success Liaison: communicates estimated timelines and evidence delivery to customer contacts. (Owner: Customer Success)

Pre-rollback requirements checklist (MUST):

1) Authorization
   - IC confirmed rollback authorization per escalation policy and legal holds.
   - Customer notification requirement verified (contract SLA/notice windows).

2) Snapshot & Telemetry
   - Configure and snapshot the following before any change:
     * Control plane manifests (kubectl get all, service, deployment, statefulset YAMLs)
     * Runtime KV/cache state pointers (if accessible)
     * Model bundle metadata (version hashes, quantization profile id)
     * Active routing and traffic-split configs

3) Evidence Store availability
   - Evidence store (internal secured S3 or EFS) reachable and writable.
   - HSM/KMS signing key(s) ready and accessible with audit logging enabled.

4) Time synchronization
   - NTP sync verified on control plane and nodes (clock skew <= 500ms).

5) Stakeholder notification
   - Customer Success and Security notified with rollback window and evidence expectations.

Minimum artifacts to capture (examples and commands)

- Cluster & control plane state:
  - kubectl get all --all-namespaces -o yaml > pre-rollback-cluster-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.yaml
  - kubectl get configmap,secret --all-namespaces -o yaml > pre-rollback-configs-...yaml

- Deployed binary/model artifacts and metadata:
  - List deployed model bundles with checksums: curl -sS http://runtime-api/models | jq . > pre-rollback-models.json
  - For each model artifact: sha256sum model-file.bin > model-file.bin.sha256

- Logs and traces window:
  - Export logs for window [-10min, +0]: elasticsearch/stack dump or journaldctl --since
  - Tracing spans export (if tracing backend supports snapshot) for the same window

- Traffic & routing configuration:
  - Snapshot ingress and service-mesh routes: istioctl proxy-config routes --all-namespaces > routes.txt

- Operational actions manifest (operator must create):
  - operator-actions-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.md (freeform list of commands to run)

Evidence preservation and signing procedure (step-by-step)

1) Collect artifacts into a dedicated evidence bundle directory named with ISO timestamp and incident id:
   - Example: evidence/INC-20260610-0001/20260610T153200/

2) For each artifact:
   - Compute SHA256 checksum and append to a checksums file: sha256sum artifact > artifact.sha256
   - Record artifact metadata: filename, source host, service, earliest and latest timestamps captured

3) Create a manifest.jsonl (one JSON per line) summarizing artifacts. Manifest fields (flat): artifact_name, checksum_sha256, collected_by, host, captured_start, captured_end, purpose
   - NOTE: If your tooling cannot produce JSONL, use newline-delimited key:value pairs in the manifest and include a schema header.

4) Sign the manifest with the HSM-backed key and store the signature alongside the manifest:
   - Example (HSM-backed PKCS#11): 
     pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so -l --sign --input-file manifest.jsonl --output-file manifest.jsonl.sig --key-label "evidence-key"

5) Upload artifact bundle to Evidence Store with server-side encryption and object immutability:
   - aws s3 cp --acl private --sse aws:kms evidence/INC-... s3://redwood-evidence/<inc-id>/ --metadata incident-id=<inc-id> --storage-class STANDARD_IA

6) Record chain-of-custody entry in the internal evidence ledger (app) or a signed ledger file:
   - Record fields (flat): incident_id, artifact_path, uploader, upload_timestamp, evidence_store_uri, signature_uri

Rollback execution patterns (safe categories)

- Configuration rollback (safe, fast):
  1. Revert the ConfigMap/Ingress/service-mesh route to pre-rollback YAML.
  2. Apply in single transaction where possible.
  3. Verify control plane health and incremental traffic shift back to expected state.

- Model or runtime binary rollback (stateful concerns):
  1. Drain traffic using service mesh weight shift (10% increments) to minimize impact.
  2. Re-deploy previous model bundle or binary into a shadow pool.
  3. Warm caches/kv pointers and validate inference correctness on canary subset.
  4. Promote to full traffic when verified.

- Full node/image rollback (destructive):
  1. Preserve node-level forensic snapshots (disk images, system logs) before wiping.
  2. Use immutable artifact promotion: do not modify the original image; deploy an explicit previous image tag.

Rollback step-by-step (canonical flow)

1) IC declares rollback and selects rollback type.
2) Run pre-rollback checklist; do NOT execute rollback until Evidence Custodian confirms evidence store readiness.
3) Collect and sign pre-rollback artifacts as described above.
4) Execute rollback using chosen pattern (config/model/node). Capture operator actions line-by-line into actions manifest.
5) During rollback, stream minimal real-time audit entries to evidence ledger: action,start_ts,actor,command_hash
6) After rollback completes, collect post-rollback artifacts (same set as pre-rollback) and sign them.
7) Compare pre/post checksums and record differences in the manifest (delta report).
8) Lock the evidence bundle (apply immutability flag) and notify Security + Customer Success.

Evidence retention table (recommended minima)

- Artifact Type | Retention (default) | Storage class | Rationale
- Cluster manifests | 7 years | Object store / WORM | Regulatory auditing (finance/health sectors)
- Signed manifests & signatures | 7 years | WORM / cold storage | Verifiable chain-of-custody
- Forensic node images | 1 year (or legal hold) | Encrypted cold | Large size; preserve if requested by legal
- Logs & traces (raw) | 90 days | Hot + warm | Operational debugging; long-term archived aggregates retained 7 years
- Action manifest & operator notes | 7 years | WORM | Human readable audit evidence

Storage and access controls

- Access to evidence store must be role-based (only Evidence Custodian, Security leads, and Legal).
- All retrieval requests logged with justification and requestor. Retrieval must be authorized by Security.
- Evidence uploads must use server-side encryption (customer-managed keys if contract requires).
- Apply object immutability (S3 Object Lock) or equivalent retained/locked state immediately after upload.

Post-rollback validation and reporting

- Validation checklist:
  - SLO check: latency and error-rate for the affected routes back within 1.5x baseline within 30 minutes.
  - Functional check: Smoke test harness (include example curl assertions) against several endpoints.
  - Data consistency: KV/kcache pointer checks for drift in the first 1 hour.

- Reporting template (deliver to customer and internal audit):
  - Incident id, timeline (ISO), justification, artifacts catalog URI, signature URIs, delta summary, action manifest (redacted as necessary), verification results.

Example verification commands (illustrative)

- Cluster snapshot:
  kubectl get all --all-namespaces -o yaml > pre-rollback-cluster.yaml

- Compute checksum and sign (local example):
  sha256sum pre-rollback-cluster.yaml > pre-rollback-cluster.yaml.sha256
  gpg --armor --output pre-rollback-cluster.yaml.sig --detach-sign --local-user redwood-evidence@example.com pre-rollback-cluster.yaml

- Upload to evidence store (AWS S3 example):
  aws s3 cp ./evidence/ s3://redwood-evidence/<inc>/ --recursive --sse aws:kms --metadata incident-id=<inc>

Danger signals and abort conditions

- Ongoing data corruption detected in post-rollback checks (stop promotion and escalate).
- Missing or failed upload of any signed manifest to the evidence store (do not proceed; open a Safety Hold).
- HSM/KMS key unavailability during signing window (do not proceed without manual Security approval).

Legal holds and external requests

- If there is a legal hold or regulatory request, Evidence Custodian must snapshot and duplicate the bundle to an isolated WORM store; follow Legal team playbook for preservation and eDiscovery.

FAQs

Q: What if the evidence store is temporarily unreachable?
A: Use an encrypted local buffer with strict ACLs; sign artifacts locally and retry upload. Record buffer location and retention policy in the ledger. Do not delete buffered artifacts until uploaded and verified.

Q: Are operator commands stored verbatim?
A: Yes. Operator action manifests must include commands executed. Sensitive secrets should be redacted before upload; include redaction reasons in the manifest.

Q: Who can request evidence retrieval?
A: Security, Legal, and authorized Customer Success leads. Retrievals require a justification and are logged.

References and related reading

- Private deploy compliance and evidence checklist (internal)
- Failure isolation & rollback playbook (internal)
- Security HSM/KMS standard operating procedures

Appendix: checklist quick-reference (copyable)

- [ ] IC authorization obtained
- [ ] Evidence store reachable and HSM available
- [ ] NTP sync validated
- [ ] Pre-rollback artifacts collected and checksummed
- [ ] Manifest signed and uploaded
- [ ] Rollback executed with operator actions logged
- [ ] Post-rollback artifacts collected and signed
- [ ] Delta report produced and uploaded
- [ ] Evidence bundle locked and retrievals authorized
